what_this_is: Reader-vs-reader pairing of the per-route x402 rows in declared_vs_live.json against an independent reader's capture of the same URLs. One row per route the two readers share. This compares READER to READER. It does NOT compare the manifest's DECLARED terms to the live 402 -- that is declared_vs_live.json / ROUTE_LAYER.md, a different question.

readers.name: Quietforge Studio
readers.what_it_captured: accepts[0] as a per-entry tuple; the remaining entries as DISTINCT SETS of network/amount/asset only. EVM and base58 addresses are case-folded, which is lossy for base58.
readers.artifact_sha256_status: VERIFIED -- two digests, deliberately. The peer named 93e41204... for the 840,177-byte copy she took the 43 URLs from, and we re-fetched that published file and it matched. That version has since been SUPERSEDED in this repo by a repair recorded in ERRATA.md, so the file published here now is a different artifact with a different digest. Measured diff between the two: the 828 URLs are identical in the same order, every aggregate is identical, and exactly 13 rows differ, in two fields only (`payto_equal` and `verdict_reason`). Neither field is an input to the reader-vs-reader join, so the join below is unaffected.

third_reading_one_route.why_this_route: the one route in the table whose own verdict is AMOUNT_INDETERMINATE and whose live offer set was observed to CHANGE between readings, so a third independent reading is worth more here than anywhere else.

readings.note: this capture stored accepts[0] as a tuple and the rest as sets, so which entry carried 101665 is not recoverable from it.
re-read 45 s later and byte-identical, so the body is stable at that interval from this vantage point.

agreements: accepts length 5 on all three readings taken after 2026-11-03T23:01Z
every amount 10000 on all three of those readings
network wire order identical on Penny's, RNA's and our 2026-11-04 readings
entries 2-5 asset and payTo identical, character for character, between RNA's published tuples and our 2026-11-04 reading

one_field_that_does_not_reconcile.statement: RNA's published value for this one field is 38 hex digits -- 19 bytes -- which is not a valid EVM address length; every other EVM value in RNA's own reading is 40. The value we read is 40 hex digits and is EIP-55 checksum-valid. Deleting the two characters 'c7' at offset 21 of our value yields RNA's value exactly.
one_field_that_does_not_reconcile.why_the_bytes_say_this_is_a_transcriptio: RNA reports 5,468 raw bytes, the same count we read. The asset value appears verbatim as a JSON string in the body, so a body carrying RNA's 38-digit value would be 5,466 bytes. 5,468 is consistent with the 40-digit value, not with RNA's transcription of it.
one_field_that_does_not_reconcile.what_we_cannot_settle: RNA's raw-body sha256 differs from ours while the byte count is equal, and our stability test covers 45 seconds, not the 69 minutes between the two captures. So we cannot exclude a length-preserving change to the body in that window. Either way the 38-digit string is not what any reader could have been served.
one_field_that_does_not_reconcile.not_a_misprice: every reading agrees the price is a uniform 10000 atomic units. Nothing here says this host charges other than it publishes.

limits: This is READER vs READER. Two agreeing readers establish that a host served the same accepts[0] to two vantage points. They establish nothing about whether the manifest's DECLARED terms match the live charge.

Our capture holds ONE genuine per-entry tuple (accepts[0]); the remaining entries are distinct SETS. So index 0 is pairable and the remainder is not, and every graded row reports our_other_entries_unpairable.

Our census case-folds addresses. A case-only difference in a base58 value is therefore not assertable from our side and is WITHHELD with the reason printed -- we cannot prove no real case-only difference is hidden by that fold.
Ordering stability is only testable where both arrays hold 2 or more entries.

A sha256 pins BYTES, not WHEN. Every reading here carries its capture instant for that reason; two readings of one host taken at different instants can differ because the host changed, not because a reader is wrong.
One vantage point per reader. An offer set or an outage seen from one network path is not a global fact.
No host in this document is named as mispriced, and none of these readings supports such a claim.
